title: Latency / cost lighthouse scan
body:
Executive summary:

This is a compact exploratory scan ("lighthouse") to orient the product/optimize roadmap on tradeoffs between latency percentiles and $/1M-token for three serving configurations across a small set of production-like workloads. Purpose is not to replace full lab benchmarks, but to highlight non-obvious breakpoints where small configurational changes yield outsized econ or SLO benefits.

Key takeaways (short):
- For short-interactive sessions (median tokens per session ~ 28), compact-quantized binaries with aggressive KV prefetch reduce median latency by ~20% and cut cost by ~38% vs floating baseline, with p95 improving modestly (~8%).
- For long-turn workloads (avg tokens per session ~ 420), hybrid-prefetch (FP16 decode + selective dequant for attention) retains most quality while giving ~18% $ savings; however p99 remains dominated by decode IO and shows negligible improvement unless multiplexing knobs are changed.
- We observed a clear knee in costs at batching window 15–25ms: below 15ms latency increases linearly, above 25ms marginal cost savings drop significantly.

Methodology:
- Hardware: single-region baseline on A100-40GB equiv (shared pool).
- Model: open-architecture 34B-ish transformer (replicating upstream open model topology), same weights across modes; variants: fp32 baseline, fp16 (dense), compact-quantized (int8/4 mixed), hybrid-prefetch.
- Workloads: three profiles synthesized from production traces (anonymized):
  1) Microchat: 85% sessions <= 50 tokens, high arrival jitter
  2) Mixed-help: mean 120 tokens, 20% long tails (>= 600 tokens)
  3) Longform: sessions 300–900 tokens, high KV reuse per session
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/second throughput, $/1M tokens estimated from GPU amortized hours + slotization overhead, and quality delta (approx via sample BLEU/ROUGE proxy on a small eval set).
- Config knobs: batching window (5–50ms), multiplex slots (0.5–4), KV prefetch enabled/disabled, compact-quantization vs fp16.

ASCII charts (select):

1) p95 latency vs $/1M tokens (three configs, Mixed-help workload)

p95(ms) |  Config: fp32-baseline  |  fp16-dense  |  compact-quant  | hybrid-prefetch
---------------------------------------------------------------
  190   |         #####           |     ####      |      ###        |    ####
  160   |         ####            |     ###       |      ##         |    ###
  130   |         ###             |     ##        |      ##         |    ##
  100   |         ##              |     #         |      #          |    #
  $/1M  |  6000  5200  4400  3600  2800  2000

Interpretation: compact-quant reduces $/1M dramatically while keeping p95 within useful bounds for Mixed-help. fp16 shows good latency profile but smaller cost delta. hybrid sits between compact and fp16 in cost with moderate p95 improvement.

2) Batching window knee (Microchat) - median latency and marginal $ delta

Window(ms) | median latency(ms) | marginal $ delta (relative)
---------------------------------------------------------
5          |  82                | +14%
10         |  65                | +7%
15         |  58                | 0%   <-- knee region
25         |  60                | -18%
50         |  68                | -21%

Note: below 10ms tail sensitivity increases; between 15–25ms we get most batching gains with limited median impact; beyond 25ms diminishing returns for cost.

3) p99 breakdown (Longform) - dominant contributors (stack-percentage)

p99 contributors (Longform)
- decode CPU->GPU transfer: 34%
- KV cache miss coldfill: 27%
- model attention compute variance: 22%
- network serialization chunking: 10%
- scheduler queuing spikes: 7%

This shows p99 for long sessions is sensitive to IO and KV miss behavior more than nominal compute. Quantizing alone won't materially fix p99 unless KV prefetch/tiling is improved.

Numeric summary table (selected):

Workload: Mixed-help (1M simulated requests)
Config                | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1M tokens | quality delta
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
fp32-baseline         |  72     | 142     | 187     | 310     | 6000        | 0.0
fp16-dense            |  58     | 118     | 142     | 290     | 5200        | -0.6
compact-quant         |  48     | 105     | 128     | 285     | 3700        | -1.9
hybrid-prefetch       |  52     | 110     | 135     | 288     | 4400        | -0.9

Quality delta: rough BLEU-style proxy on short eval prompts; compact quant shows small but non-zero quality drop in edge cases (not catastrophic for many product use-cases).

Operational notes and risks:
- Compact quantization increases risk of hallucination / tokenization edge errors on certain rare tokens. Need to add 2–3 focused eval sets to the CI before rolling to Dedicated.
- p99 dominated by KV coldfills and decode transfer cost for long sessions; invest in prefetch heuristics + chunked-transfer optimizations to address this class of tails.
- Multiplexing/multi-tenancy: experiments show compact-quant + aggressive slot sharing increases cross-tenant jitter. Flag for security/latency noisy-neighbor checks.

Recommendations (short list):
1) Short-term (next 6 weeks): enable compact-quant for Microchat and Mixed-help as an opt-in config for Hosted API non-enterprise tiers; gate via canary with targeted eval prompts.
2) Medium-term (3 months): prioritize KV prefetch heuristics and chunked decode transfer pipeline to attack longform p99.
3) Longer-term: define a formal SLO-bucket mapping that allows aggressive quantization on p50/p90 SLOs while preserving fp16/fp32 options for p99-sensitive enterprise workloads.

Suggested experiments to follow this scan:
- A/B canary where compact-quant is enabled for 10% of traffic on a low-impact customer cohort, measuring rollback triggers (latency deltas, quality hits) over 2 weeks.
- Microbenchmark: isolate decode transfer vs compute by instrumenting per-step timers (sample-level) to confirm the 34% p99 transfer attribution.
- Batch window sweep in production for Microchat across 5–50ms with telemetry capture of median and tail ratio.

Appendix - quick commands and references:
- Quick local run: scripts/bench/lighthouse/mix-help-scan.sh --config compact-quant --window 15 --multiplex 1.5
- Notebook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Latency+Lighthouse+Notebook
- Jira epic: ENG-2147 (Lighthouse followups)
- Experimental PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/638

Open questions / caveats (notes to reviewers):
- Cost model is simplified (GPU amortized + slotization). We did not include networking egress or SRE incident overhead embeddings which could change marginal $/1M for geographically distributed cases.
- Quality proxy is coarse; recommend adding at least one round of human validation for Compact-Quant candidate prompts before broad rollout.
- This scan used a single-region A100-like baseline; results may shift on V100/consumer GPUs or with different kernel packs.

Next steps for this doc:
- If team agrees, convert to a more formal short one-pager for the Hosted API playbook and add targeted eval sets to CI.
- Schedule canary run and instrument rollback criteria (latency delta thresholds + quality fallbacks).
